description: We are tackling the Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots challenge by building an instrument-aware calibration pipeline in Python. Using spatial binning (scan × track optical geometry), orbital de-duplication, and Gradient Boosting with Duan’s smearing estimator, we eliminate the 2012 sensor transition bias to deliver a robust 26-year fire activity time series (2000–2026) across Chile.
summary: Project CHILE-FIRE (2000–2026) is an open source, interactive satellite intelligence and civic prevention platform built with 26 years of NASA FIRMS thermal observations across all 16 regions of Chile. Raw multi-decade fire records suffer from a major sensor discontinuity when transitioning from 1 km MODIS (2000–2011) to 375 m VIIRS (2012–2026), creating artificial upward jumps that distort historical baselines. We solved this by building a machine-learning harmonization pipeline (orbital deduplication, scan-by-track pixel geometry correction, and Gradient Boosting with Duan smearing calibration, achieving R² = 0.887 and +4.88% blind hindcast bias) that aligns 26 years of hotspots and Fire Radiative Power (MW) onto a unified scale. Through a mobile-friendly, accessible 5-step dashboard (featuring colorblind-safe palettes, large text, and audio summaries), citizens identify their neighborhood's critical 3-month wildfire window and generate pre-filled preventive firebreak requests to CONAF, SENAPRED, and local municipalities, while planners export QGIS ready geospatial datasets.
details:
Project Chile-fire (2000–2026) transforms 26 years of raw NASA Earth observation fire detections into an intuitive, 5-step decision and civic-action tool covering all 16 administrative regions of Chile:

1. Multi Sensor Scientific Harmonization: Direct comparison of historical MODIS (1 km resolution, 2000–2011) and modern VIIRS (375 m resolution, 2012–2026) records produces an artificial step-change due to finer spatial sensitivity. Using the 14 year sensor overlap period, we implemented orbital pass deduplication, optical pixel-stretching correction (scan × track), and a Gradient Boosting regressor with Duan smearing retransformation (Linear R² = 0.887; blind 2012–2015 hindcast R² = 0.784 with only +4.88% bias) to reconstruct consistent historical hotspots and Fire Radiative Power (FRP in MW).

2. Adaptive 5 Step Interface for Three Audiences: Users select any region in Chile (with exact polygonal boundaries) and switch between Citizens (Simple), Municipalities (QGIS), and Researchers (Data) profiles, inspecting any year, quarter, or specific month against a 26-year median baseline.

3. Interactive Satellite Mapping & Reverse Geocoding: A 26 year heatmap calendar (2026 down to 2000) pairs with an interactive Esri World Imagery map (bubbles, density heatmaps, or gridded cells with 5 km / 10 km proximity buffers). Clicking any hotspot triggers reverse geocoding to identify the exact commune, rural sector, or reserve.

4. From Data to Preventive Action: For citizens, the platform automatically computes the neighborhood's top 3 critical fire months and generates a 1 click pre filled email (`mailto:`) and copyable letter addressed to CONAF, SENAPRED, and municipal emergency offices requesting preventive brush clearing and firebreaks before peak season. Municipal and scientific users can export calibrated CSV files with exact coordinates (`lat_exact`, `lon_exact`) ready for QGIS.

Benefits & Intended Impact

Chile faces recurring catastrophic wildland-urban interface fires (such as Biobío 2023 and Valparaíso February 2024). By translating complex satellite time series into localized seasonal risk windows, this tool empowers everyday residents, neighborhood associations, and municipal planners to demand and schedule preventive firebreaks months before peak fire weather arrives, while providing immediate emergency guidance (130 CONAF / 132 Firefighters / SAE protocols).

Tools, Languages & Software Used

Languages & Core Libraries: Python, pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn (Gradient Boosting Regressor).

Visualization & Web App: Streamlit, Plotly (interactive heatmaps, confidence-band time series, and geospatial maps).

Geospatial & Accessibility APIs: OpenStreetMap Nominatim Reverse Geocoding API, Esri World Imagery raster tiles, and the browser Web Speech API for bilingual (Spanish/English) audio narration.

Creativity & Design Considerations

False Positive Industrial Filtering:Automatically identifies and toggles off persistent year-round thermal anomalies in northern Chile's Atacama Desert (copper smelters and concentrated solar power plants) so wildfire statistics remain accurate.

Inclusive Universal Accessibility: Built with a colorblind-safe `Cividis` palette toggle, a large typography mode for older adults, audio summaries for visually impaired users, screenreader accessible data tables, and responsive mobile-first layouts.

Super Intelligence (SI) Transparency Disclosure

In accordance with NASA Space Apps Challenge guidelines, generative AI / Super Intelligence (LLM coding assistance) was used to accelerate Python/Streamlit UI refactoring, responsive CSS layout styling, and English/Spanish bilingual localization. All scientific data processing, sensor calibration methodology, validation metrics, and geospatial architecture were designed, verified, and executed by the team. No NASA logos or brand emblems were generated or modified using SI tools.
